external_entities.name: customer user
external_entities.description: A person at a customer company who uses the billing app as an admin or viewer.
external_entities.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
external_entities.notes: Users are either admins or viewers. Authentication uses an email address, password, and session cookie; there is no second factor.

external_entities.name: payer
external_entities.description: The recipient of an invoice email who accesses the payment page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
external_entities.notes: The payer is not required to sign in.

external_entities.name: support agent
external_entities.description: An agent who operates from the support office network and uses the admin console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.
external_entities.notes: Each agent signs in with their own account and a one-time code. Actions in the billing app are recorded against the customer user rather than the agent.

processes.name: billing app
processes.description: The shared invoicing application used by customer users, payers, and support agents.
processes.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app
processes.notes: The app applies company filters to database queries itself, loads invoices by invoice number, saves all submitted invoice fields, enqueues render jobs, and fetches PDFs.

processes.name: PDF renderer
processes.description: A renderer that consumes render jobs, reads invoices, and writes PDFs.
processes.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
processes.notes: The renderer trusts the company ID carried by a job.

processes.name: admin console
processes.description: The console used by support agents to open billing-app sessions as customer users.
processes.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
processes.notes: The console is reachable only from the support office network. Its runtime location is not stated.

data_stores.name: tenant database
data_stores.description: A shared PostgreSQL database containing every company's invoices, customers, and payout bank details.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database, the tenant database.
data_stores.notes: Every table has a company ID column. The database has no row-level security and the app uses one database account for all companies.

data_stores.name: render queue
data_stores.description: A queue holding PDF render jobs containing a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: To make a PDF, the billing app puts a render job on the render queue.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state how the queue is reached or protected.

data_stores.name: PDF bucket
data_stores.description: A shared cloud bucket containing rendered PDFs stored under company IDs and invoice numbers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state how the bucket is reached or protected at rest.

data_flows.name: use billing app
data_flows.description: A customer user uses the billing app in a browser over HTTPS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
data_flows.authentication: email address and password; session cookie; no second factor
data_flows.data_description: Authentication credentials, session cookie, invoices, customer information, and payout bank details

data_flows.name: query tenant data
data_flows.description: The billing app queries the tenant database using a company filter.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app adds the company filter to each query itself
data_flows.notes: The app connects with one database account for all companies.
data_flows.authentication: one database account for all companies
data_flows.data_description: Invoices, customers, payout bank details, and invoice changes

data_flows.name: open invoice
data_flows.description: A customer user opens an invoice using its invoice number.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a user opens an invoice, the billing app loads it by its invoice number.
data_flows.notes: It is unknown whether the app checks that the invoice belongs to the user's company.
data_flows.data_description: Invoice number and invoice contents

data_flows.name: edit invoice
data_flows.description: A customer user submits the whole invoice to the billing app for saving.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The invoice edit form posts the whole invoice back
data_flows.notes: The billing app saves every field it receives, including the paid flag and payout bank account. It is unknown whether the user's role is checked again when the request arrives.
data_flows.data_description: Whole invoice, paid flag, and payout bank account

data_flows.name: send invoice email
data_flows.description: The billing app sends the payer an invoice link ending in the invoice number.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
data_flows.data_description: Invoice link containing an invoice number

data_flows.name: view payment page
data_flows.description: The payer follows the invoice link and views the payment page.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The payment page shows the invoice, the company's name and its bank details
data_flows.notes: The payment page asks the payer to sign in to nothing.
data_flows.data_description: Invoice, company name, and payout bank details

data_flows.name: request PDF
data_flows.description: A user requests a PDF of an invoice.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Any user can ask for a PDF of any invoice, as often as they like.
data_flows.data_description: Invoice number and PDF request

data_flows.name: enqueue render job
data_flows.description: The billing app places a render job on the render queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The job carries a company ID and an invoice number.
data_flows.data_description: Company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: read render job
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer takes render jobs from the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
data_flows.data_description: Render job containing company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: read invoice
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer reads the invoice from the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: reads the invoice from the tenant database
data_flows.data_description: Invoice identified by company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: write PDF
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer writes a PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and invoice number.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number.
data_flows.notes: The renderer trusts the company ID carried by the job.
data_flows.data_description: Rendered invoice PDF, company ID, and invoice number

data_flows.name: fetch PDFs
data_flows.description: The billing app fetches PDFs from the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.
data_flows.authentication: one service credential for all companies
data_flows.data_description: Rendered invoice PDFs

data_flows.name: use admin console
data_flows.description: A support agent signs in to and uses the admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: each agent signs in to it with their own account and a one-time code.
data_flows.notes: The admin console is reachable only from the support office network.
data_flows.data_description: Admin-console credentials and customer-user information

data_flows.name: open customer session
data_flows.description: The admin console opens a billing-app session as any customer user.
data_flows.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
data_flows.data_description: Customer-user session and customer-user identity

data_flows.name: record user actions
data_flows.description: The billing app records actions in the tenant database against the customer user.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Everything the agent then does is recorded in the tenant database against that customer user, and not against the agent.
data_flows.data_description: Recorded customer-user actions

trust_boundaries.name: customer company
trust_boundaries.description: The customer-company tenant zone containing customer users.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant

trust_boundaries.name: cloud platform
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud-platform zone containing the shared billing app, tenant database, render queue, PDF renderer, and PDF bucket.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform.

trust_boundaries.name: support office network
trust_boundaries.description: The support-office network from which support agents work and the admin console is reachable.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.

assumptions.assumption: The tenant database contains confidential data because it stores customer information, invoices, and payout bank details.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly states that the database stores invoices, customers, and payout bank details.

assumptions.assumption: The PDF bucket contains confidential data because it stores rendered invoice PDFs, which represent invoices and may show company and bank details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the bucket stores PDFs rendered from invoices, and the payment page includes company and bank details.

assumptions.assumption: The cloud platform is a network trust boundary for the components explicitly described as being in that platform.
assumptions.basis: The source places the shared billing app, database, and PDF bucket in a cloud platform; the render components are modelled in that same platform as the described service infrastructure.
